ARPENOS Python baseline provenance and limits
===========================================

Author code: Frederic Sur and Michel Grediac, ARPENOS v1.2, August 2016.
Author page: https://members.loria.fr/FSur/software/ARPENOS/
Original files: ARPENOS.m, sym_conv2.m, ARPENOS_example.m.
Downloaded: 2026-11-16. author_page.html preserves the public usage terms.
Usage condition on the author page: "The following codes can be used for
academic research only". Retain this restriction and cite the original authors
when using or redistributing the derivative for this course project. This is
not an unrestricted open-source license. No authors' photographs are bundled.

Citation:
F. Sur and M. Grediac. Automated removal of quasiperiodic noise using frequency
domain statistics. Journal of Electronic Imaging 24(1), 013003 (2015).
DOI: 10.1117/1.JEI.24.1.013003.

published_baseline.py ports the default reg=0 path of the author code. It keeps
the patch Hanning window, 1/8 stride, geometric mean power spectrum, f0=2/L,
f1=0.2, f2=8/L, 3-sigma detection, bilinear frequency interpolation, Gaussian
notch construction, conjugate symmetrization and noise-subtraction pipeline.
The original patch-loop endpoint convention is retained.

Explicit differences:
1. MATLAB robustfit (default bisquare) and its stats.s are replaced by a
   documented bisquare IRLS implementation with leverage adjustment and MAD
   scale. This can change the outlier set and the final output. The port has
   NOT been numerically compared to MATLAB and must not be called bitwise
   equivalent or used to claim replication of the paper's reported numbers.
2. The optional TV regularization path (reg=1) is not included. Baseline names
   must say ARPENOS Python reg0 or ARPENOS source-guided port, not AC-ARPENOS.
3. Plotting and console statements are omitted; diagnostics are returned.
4. A positive float floor prevents log(0), a common-power scaling prevents
   exponent overflow, and constant images return unchanged. These safeguards
   differ from the original's possible nonfinite behavior.
5. Odd-sized images use true FFT coordinates; the original centered frequency
   axis assumes even dimensions. Experiments use even dimensions.
6. Returned images are not clipped or contrast-normalized. The caller chooses
   evaluation clipping consistently across all compared methods.

The original example uses patch size 128. At 256-pixel input size, patch size
64 is an experiment setting, not a paper default. f2=8/L prevents detection
below 0.125 cycles/pixel when L=64, so L=128 is preferable if the input permits.
